h1:
Korat Mookata
10 Best-Value Thai BBQ Buffets
intro: Cool season in Korat means dinner around the grill — sizzling pork, a punchy dipping sauce, the whole table leaning in. This city has mookata and BBQ buffet joints in just about every neighbourhood, from 99 THB a grill up to full seafood lines. We picked 10 spots that locals actually go to, with straight talk on prices and where to find them.

blocks.html: Mookata is the dinner Korat locals meet up over — with a group of friends, the family, or treating the team after work. What sets this city apart is the sheer number of places and how hard they compete on price, so you eat your fill on a lighter budget than in a lot of provinces. Some spots are under 100 THB a grill; others go all in on seafood with river prawns and oysters. We've split it up so it's easy to scan — from budget picks to seafood spreads to Korean BBQ.

blocks.text: 10 mookata & BBQ buffets Korat locals actually go to

blocks.html: Ordered mainly by how often locals mention them and how much value you get. Prices are approximate as of early 2026 and can shift with whatever promo is running, so check the restaurant's page before you go.

items.name: Kaen Chan Premium (Night Ban Ko / Talad Hello)
items.blurb: The first name Korat locals think of for mookata in town. This one is set-menu rather than all-you-can-eat — fresh ingredients, a punchy, full-flavoured dipping sauce, plus free refills on veggies, watermelon and ice cream. It gets packed in the evening, so go early or be ready to queue.
items.price: Small set ฿150 (buy 2 get 1 free) · large set ฿200

items.name: Im Suk Mookata Buffet
items.blurb: A no-time-limit buffet that's easy on the wallet and gets a lot of reviews. It's on the road behind The Mall, open and airy, with a wide spread — beef, pork, chicken, seafood, meatballs, veggies and desserts. Several broths and dipping sauces to choose from. The bit people love: drink refills are just 19 THB, so the total bill still works out cheap.
items.meta: Behind The Mall Korat · no time limit

items.name: Pa Ko Mookata & Seafood Buffet, Hua Thale
items.blurb: If you're here for seafood, this is the one. The line goes all the way to salmon steak, river prawns, oysters, marinated raw crab and desserts. The price includes drinks and there's no time limit on your table. Good for when you want to eat seriously or it's a special occasion.
items.meta: Soi Lotus Hua Thale · open 4:00 PM–11:00 PM

items.name: Boss Shabu BBQ Pen Tor Buffet
items.blurb: The cheapest on the list — under 100 THB a grill — with shabu, BBQ and mookata all in one pot. Good for students and anyone on a tight budget around Suranaree. Don't expect premium ingredients, but you'll leave full and it's solid value at this price.

items.name: Yuki-chan Buffet Mookata & Grilled Seafood
items.blurb: Across from The Sefcom, so it's easy to reach. It's a mookata buffet with grilled seafood — prawns, shellfish and squid to grill yourself. Good for groups after an evening browsing the Sefcom night market.
items.price: Buffet from a couple hundred baht

items.name: Siam Buffet Mookata & Grilled Seafood (Pak Thong Chai)
items.blurb: The pick for people around Pak Thong Chai and anyone driving the Korat–Kabin Buri route. A buffet with grilled seafood plus free drink refills, and a well-stocked line. Good to stop at before heading into Khao Yai or on the way back from a trip.

items.name: Rabieng Shabu
items.blurb: For shabu fans who want a big spread — over 50 items, including beef, river prawns, sliced pork, squid, grilled sausage, snacks and desserts. Korean-style broths and dipping sauces, no time limit, drink refills included.
items.meta: In Korat town · no time limit

items.name: Mookata at Sefcom Night Market
items.blurb: Mookata in a night-market setting — wander, shop, then sit down for a long meal. You can go mookata-only or add a BBQ grill. Cheap, no time limit, good for an easygoing group outing.
items.meta: Sefcom Night Market · no time limit
items.price: Mookata ฿169 · with BBQ grill ฿189 (drinks not included)

items.name: Korean Naju BBQ
items.blurb: A Korean BBQ buffet for people who love Korean-marinated pork — pork collar, soy-marinated ribs, gochujang pork belly, with Korean side dishes and free water included. You get around 1 hour 20 minutes. Good if you want a change from Thai-style mookata.
items.meta: In town (Nai Mueang) · time limit ~1 hr 20 min

items.name: Nam Wan Korean Grilled Meat, 30 Kanya
items.blurb: A sweet price for the Korean BBQ crowd. The line is well stocked — sliced pork, pork belly, squid, fried bites and sweets. Good for student groups around Suranarai who want the Korean feel on a light budget.

blocks.title: How to pick the right spot
blocks.html: Light budget or a big group: go for Boss Pen Tor or Im Suk · craving serious seafood: Pa Ko or Siam Buffet · want the Korean feel: try Korean Naju or 30 Kanya · if you want fresh, premium ingredients ordered as a set, Kaen Chan is the answer.

blocks.text: How much does mookata cost in Korat?

blocks.html: A price overview makes it easier to plan your budget. These figures are per person and can change with each place's promo.

items: Budget (99–169 THB) — Boss Pen Tor, 30 Kanya, Sefcom. About eating your fill cheaply; ingredients may not be premium, but they're plenty for an easygoing meal.
Mid-range (199–269 THB) — Im Suk, Rabieng Shabu, Siam Buffet. A more varied spread, with grilled seafood or beef in the mix.
Full spread (299–339 THB) — Pa Ko, Korean Naju. For a special meal or a get-together, with a complete seafood or Korean BBQ line.
One more thing — many places charge separately for drink refills, 19–49 THB. Don't forget to add it to your budget.

blocks.html: Mookata in Korat is mainly a dinner thing. Most places open around 4:00–4:30 PM and start filling up after 7 PM. If you're coming with a big group or on a Friday–Saturday, go early or call to book a table.

items: Arrive before 6 PM — prime time after 7 PM means long queues, especially at Kaen Chan and the popular spots around Night Ban Ko.
Check if there's a time limit — Korean BBQ places like Korean Naju cap you at around 1 hour 20 minutes, while most mookata spots let you stay as long as you like.
Factor in drinks — some places quote a buffet price that doesn't include drinks, so ask before you order.
Easily spoiled items — seafood and fresh ingredients should be grilled through. Most places are clean, but a quick look at how fresh the line is before you serve yourself never hurts.

items.name: Big group, tight budget
items.blurb: Boss Pen Tor or Im Suk — sit as long as you like, no time limit, easy on the wallet. Good for students and anyone watching the budget.

items.name: Celebrating or treating someone
items.blurb: Pa Ko seafood buffet — river prawns, oysters, salmon. If you want to go all in this meal, it's worth it.

items.name: Want a change of pace
items.blurb: Korean Naju or 30 Kanya — Korean BBQ with marinated pork and side dishes, a switch-up from the usual mookata.

faq.q: Which mookata spot in Korat is the best value?
faq.a: By price-per-fill, Boss Shabu BBQ Pen Tor at 99 THB a grill is the lightest. For all-you-can-eat with a varied spread and good reviews, Im Suk at 199 THB plus a 19 THB drink charge is the one people talk about most, and it's great value.

faq.q: Where do I go for a seafood buffet in Korat?
faq.a: Pa Ko Mookata & Seafood Buffet at Hua Thale goes the hardest — river prawns, oysters, salmon steak and marinated raw crab, at 339 THB including drinks and with no time limit on your table. Out toward Pak Thong Chai, Siam Buffet does a grilled-seafood spread at 269 THB.

faq.q: What time do mookata places in Korat open?
faq.a: Most are dinner spots, opening around 4:00–4:30 PM and running late. Pa Ko, for example, is open 4:00–11:00 PM, and Kaen Chan runs from 4:30 PM to midnight. It gets busy after 7 PM, so go early or book a table if you're coming with a crowd.

faq.q: Is there a Korean BBQ or grilled-meat buffet in Korat?
faq.a: Yes — Korean Naju BBQ in town is a Korean BBQ buffet at 299 THB with about 1 hour 20 minutes of seating, and Nam Wan Korean Grilled Meat (30 Kanya) near Suranarai is a lighter-budget option at 129 THB. There are also several more Korean BBQ spots behind Night Ban Ko.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table for mookata in Korat?
faq.a: On a normal weekday you can usually just walk in, but popular places like Kaen Chan or the spots around Night Ban Ko get packed on Friday–Saturday. If you're coming as a big group, call to book or arrive before 6 PM so you don't wait long.
